Sublăquĕum , i, n.,
I.a little town of the Æqui, in Latium, near which Nero had a country-seat, now Subiaco, Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 109; Tac. A. 14, 22.—Hence, Sublăcen-sis , e, adj., of or belonging to Sublaqueum: “villa,” that of Nero, near Sublaqueum, Front. Aquaed. 93 : “viae,” constructed there by him, id. ib. 7 ; 14; 15.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
